name: MGM Grand Hotel & Casino
positioning: Large resort and casino on the South Strip of Las Vegas, with a pool complex with a lazy river, two-level Skylofts and recently remodeled rooms
best_for: Travelers who want a South Strip base with its own monorail stop
Groups who want a big pool scene with a lazy river and a daylife club

facts.text: The hotel sits on the South Strip, across from New York-New York, with easy access to T-Mobile Arena.
The hotel has an attached Las Vegas Monorail stop that links it to mid-Strip, the Convention Center and the north end of the Strip.
Pedestrian bridges put New York-New York, Excalibur and the T-Mobile Arena corridor within easy walking distance.
Skylofts come with residential living and dining spaces and 24-hour butler service.
The rooms have been freshly remodeled in a sleek, modern style.
The upgraded bathrooms feature walk-in glass showers.
The redesigned rooms offer views of the Strip.
Restore rooms are offered as a wellness-focused room type.
The Studio Tower rooms were redone in 2022 with a midcentury desert glam look.
The Grand Spa has saunas, whirlpools and lounges.
The resort has multiple theaters that host everything from long-running productions to rotating headliners.
The Joel Robuchon restaurant was designed to resemble an Art Deco townhouse with a garden terrace and marble floors.

highlights.text: The Grand Pool Complex has a lazy river and waterfalls.
Skylofts are two-level lofts reached by a private elevator and Sky Lobby, with double-height Strip views.
The main tower's rooms and suites completed a Gensler-led renovation in November 2025.
Wet Republic adds a dedicated daylife scene with big-name DJs.
When MGM Grand opened in 1993, it was wrapped in emerald glass and fronted by a giant lion.

considerations.text: Guests must be 21 or older to check in.
The hotel does not have an airport shuttle to Harry Reid International Airport.
WhataHotel notes that the resort's large size can mean significant walking distances.
